title: FROM THE OPENING UP
status: Storyboard and directions only; no rendered video

shots.title: The opening
shots.start_state: White stucco shell with completely empty rough opening; no sill receiver, aluminum members, glass or door.
shots.action: Camera trucks right by a short distance at fixed height and orientation. Near white pier drifts left more than the back wall. No construction action in this establishing shot.
shots.end_state: Same empty opening seen slightly farther from the right. Opening dimensions, unfinished interior and daylight unchanged.
shots.camera: 35mm-equivalent medium-wide. True rightward truck, fixed lens and level orientation. Do not pan to keep the opening centered.
shots.keyframe: Clean photorealistic 16:9 exterior medium-wide frame of the continuity storefront before any glazing work. Empty rectangular opening in white stucco, graphite fascia, pale concrete sidewalk, unfinished interior. Match the approved clean final elevation in building dimensions and position, but remove all glazing-system components. Camera just left of center, daylight upper left. No people, lettering, overlays or panel numbers.
shots.prompt: The camera translates smoothly to the right beside the empty storefront opening. The nearby white pier moves left faster than the unfinished interior back wall, creating real depth parallax. Building remains fixed and opening remains entirely empty. Fixed lens, level camera. No framing or glass appears.
shots.reject: Push-in, lens zoom, pan, digital scale, still plate, spontaneous construction, changing shell.
shots.recovery: Shorten the rightward travel and use a closer pier for visible depth. Retain the truck; never replace it with a push.

shots.title: Set the base
shots.start_state: Close view of the lower opening. A short visible portion of graphite sill receiver is supported just above its intended substrate position by gloved hands. No upright jamb already installed in this shot.
shots.action: Hands lower the rigid receiver a small distance and bring it to rest in its prepared position. One small physical placement only; do not attempt the entire sill assembly in one clip.
shots.end_state: Receiver rests stationary against its intended base position, hands still supporting it. No assertion that anchorage or weatherproofing has been completed.
shots.camera: Tripod-locked close detail, low oblique angle, receiver and substrate in same plane of focus. Zero camera movement.
shots.keyframe: Photorealistic low close-up of the base of the same white-stucco storefront opening before uprights or glass. Two work-gloved hands support a straight graphite sill receiver a small visible distance above its prepared base. Receiver and substrate gap both readable. Match pale concrete and upper-left daylight. No upright jamb, labels or numbers. Clean 16:9.
shots.prompt: Locked camera. Two gloved hands lower the straight graphite sill receiver slowly through a small visible gap until it rests in position on the prepared base. Hands maintain stable support and the metal keeps its exact rigid shape. No upright member or glass appears. Stop when contact is established.
shots.reject: Metal grows into place, base morphs, unstable hand count, floating receiver, completed jamb appears, camera drifts.
shots.recovery: Use a tighter view and shorter lowering distance. Repair start/end support poses. Keep real lowering and contact visible.

shots.title: Stand the member
shots.start_state: Sill already placed. Two installers support a rigid graphite vertical member with its bottom seated and its top slightly short of final alignment. No glass.
shots.action: Installers guide the top through a small arc into upright alignment while keeping the bottom seated. No overhead hoist, no unsupported flying member.
shots.end_state: Member is upright in its intended location and remains held. Do not imply a complete anchored frame from this one shot.
shots.camera: Locked medium oblique view; bottom seat, top alignment and both supporting workers remain visible. Fixed lens.
shots.keyframe: Clean medium view of the same shell with sill installed but no glass. Two adult installers in charcoal and gray workwear, hard hats, eye protection and gloves support one graphite aluminum member. Bottom seated on sill, top only slightly out of upright alignment; both support points visible. Match approved member proportions. No full glazed assembly or text.
shots.prompt: Locked camera. The two installers maintain contact with one rigid graphite vertical member and guide its top a small distance into upright alignment. The bottom stays seated at the same point on the sill throughout. Workers stop with the member upright and supported. Metal does not stretch or change section. No glass appears.
shots.reject: Member extrudes upward, bottom slides, floating member, faces or limbs duplicate, frame completes itself, truck or zoom.
shots.recovery: Reduce the starting lean and isolate this one alignment action. Preserve both visible support points and the locked camera.

shots.title: The frame is ready
shots.start_state: Complete aluminum frame matching approved final elevation. All fixed-lite pockets and right-side door opening empty. No people.
shots.action: A short downward camera pedestal shows the complete frame and ends emphasizing sill continuity. No new members install inside this shot.
shots.end_state: Same complete empty frame. Transom, mullions and all bays retain exact positions.
shots.camera: Level fixed-orientation downward camera translation, modest travel, no tilt or zoom. Wide enough to show empty pockets.
shots.keyframe: Straight-on clean wide view of the same storefront with the entire graphite aluminum frame now installed, including approved single transom and right-side single-door bay. All pockets empty; no glass, door or workers. Same white shell, unfinished interior and daylight. Camera slightly above final shot level to allow short downward pedestal.
shots.prompt: The camera lowers smoothly a short distance with its orientation and focal length fixed, revealing the sill relationship to the pale sidewalk. The complete aluminum frame remains rigid and unchanged. Every glass pocket and the right door bay remain empty. No workers, glass or new metal appears.
shots.reject: Glass appears, additional mullions grow, frame layout changes, upward move, tilt instead of pedestal, held still.
shots.recovery: Provide a closer foreground sill edge to make vertical parallax visible. Retain downward translation. Never substitute a tilt.

shots.title: Seat the glass
shots.start_state: One fixed bay is shown close enough to read its lower pocket. Two installers support a rigid upright clear-glass lite on suction handles; lower edge visibly a small distance above its intended supported seat. Top is already aligned for this small final seating move. Adjacent bays may remain empty.
shots.action: Both installers guide the supported lite down through the short remaining distance into its prepared seat. Glass must move relative to the fixed frame. Stop with support still maintained; no suction release required.
shots.end_state: Bottom edge is visibly seated, pane remains upright and supported, frame and lite dimensions unchanged. Do not depict unseen fastening or claim the whole bay is finished.
shots.camera: Absolutely locked medium close view. Include lower gap, rigid glass edge, fixed frame and both suction contact points. No camera motion.
shots.keyframe: Photorealistic medium close view of a fixed bay in the same graphite frame. Two consistent installers support one transparent rigid rectangular glass lite with suction handles. Show its lower edge visibly a few centimeters above the prepared lower seat, with plausible clearance and top alignment. Hands on handles, glass edge unobscured. No floating glass, unsafe load or text.
shots.prompt: Locked camera. The two installers keep both suction handles attached and lower the single rigid glass lite slowly through the short visible remaining gap into its prepared lower seat. The bottom glass edge descends relative to the stationary aluminum sill until contact is visible. The pane remains rectangular, clear, upright and supported. All other frame members stay fixed. No glass bending, dissolve, growth or camera move.
shots.reject: No relative pane/frame displacement; panel fades in; pane bends or passes through metal; handles detach; hands slide through glass; base gap concealed; zoom or moving camera.
shots.recovery: Qualify this shot before batching. Improve the clean start/end geometry and shorten travel while preserving visible lowering into the seat. Test up to two focused H3 revisions, then the same action with another installed suitable model. Report failure rather than replace with a stationary panel or camera move.

shots.title: Finish the joint
shots.start_state: Fixed lite already installed. Macro view of a short unfinished straight perimeter joint; nozzle positioned at its starting end. Other installation and retention operations happened between cuts.
shots.action: A gloved hand moves the nozzle left to right, laying one short continuous bead only where the nozzle has passed. The bead grows from contact with the nozzle, not by an independent animated line.
shots.end_state: One short neat bead remains behind the nozzle. Existing glass and aluminum stay fixed.
shots.camera: Tripod-locked macro with a shallow but readable focus plane along the joint. No sweep, push or zoom.
shots.keyframe: Clean photorealistic macro of a straight perimeter joint between installed clear glass and graphite aluminum on the same storefront. A gloved hand holds a sealant applicator nozzle at the left start of a short unfilled joint. Nozzle contact and remaining joint visible. Fine material texture, no words or diagrams.
shots.prompt: Locked macro camera. A gloved hand guides the applicator nozzle steadily from left to right along the short fixed glass-to-aluminum joint. One continuous small sealant bead remains immediately behind the moving nozzle. The glass and frame do not move, and the bead appears only where the nozzle has passed. No floating luminous line or camera movement.
shots.reject: Bead appears ahead of nozzle, nozzle floats, joint moves, tools melt, wrong travel direction, camera sweep.
shots.recovery: Use a shorter straight joint and slower hand travel. Keep nozzle contact readable. Rerender instead of adding a graphic line.

shots.title: Fit the entrance
shots.start_state: Surrounding fixed glass complete. Right-side door leaf is upright, supported at its bottom and by both installers using suction handles; hinge edge slightly separated from its jamb. Door support remains in frame.
shots.action: Workers translate the supported rigid door leaf a small distance toward the hinge jamb to bring it into alignment. This is fitting/alignment, not a complete hinge installation or door-swing demonstration.
shots.end_state: Door leaf is aligned beside its hinge jamb with support maintained. Hardware fastening is omitted by the following edit, not generated magically.
shots.camera: Locked medium shot of right door bay, including leaf, jamb, workers and bottom support. No orbit, truck or zoom.
shots.keyframe: Clean medium shot of the right door bay of the same storefront, fixed glazing complete. Two consistent installers support an upright graphite-framed glass door on a visible bottom support with suction handles. Door hinge edge is a small visible distance away from its final jamb alignment. Both leaf and jamb readable; door not already attached or swinging. No extra door or text.
shots.prompt: Locked camera. The installers keep the upright framed glass door supported at its bottom and on both suction handles. Together they translate the rigid door leaf a small distance toward the fixed hinge jamb until the hinge-side edges align. Keep its height, rectangular shape, glass and support stable. Stop with support maintained. No swinging, floating leaf, automatic hinge attachment or camera movement.
shots.reject: Door swings instead of translating; already fitted leaf merely held; bottom unsupported; door passes through jamb; handles or hands detach; hinges grow; camera moves.
shots.recovery: Qualify this shot before batching. Repair visible support and starting clearance, shorten translation, and keep the identical alignment action. After two focused revisions test another installed suitable model on the same action. An attractive door swing or held pose is not a pass.

shots.title: The finished storefront
shots.start_state: All glazing and final door installation complete between cuts. Door closed, tools and crew gone, interior lights on. Same exterior daylight and approved frame layout.
shots.action: Camera pulls backward smoothly, widening the view of the finished facade with real depth parallax. Door stays closed and glass fixed.
shots.end_state: Complete finished storefront is readable as a whole. Same white piers, two fixed bays, transom and right-side single door. No change of time or location.
shots.camera: 35mm-equivalent three-quarter wide, true backward dolly, level fixed orientation and focal length. Near pier recedes differently from interior.
shots.keyframe: Photorealistic finished version of the approved storefront elevation, viewed from a modest exterior three-quarter angle. White stucco shell, graphite fascia, exact locked mullion positions, clear fixed glass, one closed right-hand door, pale sidewalk. Interior lights on, plausible daylight reflections with transparency. No workers, tools, signs or generated logo. Clean 16:9 with room for real backward camera travel.
shots.prompt: The camera dollies backward smoothly from the finished glass storefront, revealing more of the same white facade and pale sidewalk through real depth parallax. Near pier edges recede relative to the interior. Fixed focal length, level orientation. All glazing remains rigid and installed, the right-side door stays closed, and daylight is unchanged. No lens zoom, digital scaling or scene transformation.
shots.reject: Digital zoom out, held plate, pan, changed facade, extra door, shifting mullions, new furniture or sudden sunset.
shots.recovery: Reduce pullback distance and include a nearer pier edge for parallax. Keep the actual backward dolly and unchanged architecture.
